watchers.name: cli-commands
watchers.detect: New or renamed command names from `program.command()` / Commander definitions. New or removed flags from `.option()`. Argument signature changes. Help-text changes.

watchers.name: env-vars
watchers.detect: Lines matching `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*=` in .env.example; `process.env.X` reads; zod env schema fields. Append-only edits are auto-merge; renames/removals escalate to PR tier.

watchers.name: rest-routes
watchers.detect: Route registrations (`app.get/post/put/delete`, fastify `route({...})`). New route file = new doc page; signature/payload changes = update existing page.

watchers.name: adapters
watchers.detect: Files under packages/adapters/<name>/** or packages/plugins/sandbox-providers/<name>/** signal adapter changes. The <name> at depth 1 identifies the adapter. New top-level <name> dir = candidate new adapter — but first consult scripts/sync/detect-renames.mjs to confirm it's not a directory rename. Rename = update existing doc page in place with change_kind: renamed; genuinely-new = create a new page mirroring the neighbour pattern. Manifest (`package.json`, `adapter.json`) changes = update existing page.

watchers.name: plugin-sdk
watchers.detect: Public API surface of the plugin SDK — exported types/functions from src/index.ts. The reference page (docs/reference/plugins/sdk.md) is the canonical home; docs/administration/plugins.md may need touch-ups when the operator-facing usage flow changes. (If the SDK package dir itself is renamed, consult scripts/sync/detect-renames.mjs before treating the new path as a fresh surface.)

watchers.name: agent-skills
watchers.detect: Any file under skills/** in parent — these are canonical skill bundles. New top-level dir under skills/ = candidate new skill bundle (consult scripts/sync/detect-renames.mjs to confirm it's not a rename of an existing bundle before creating a new doc entry); mention in the skills reference. Changes inside an existing bundle = update the tutorial or reference as appropriate. The plugin SDK is a separate concern — see the plugin-sdk watcher. The app-shipped skills catalog is a separate concern — see the skills-catalog watcher.

watchers.name: skills-catalog
watchers.detect: The app-shipped skills catalog — installable bundled/optional skills, distinct from the server-forced bundled skills under skills/** (covered by the agent-skills watcher). Skill bundles live at packages/skills-catalog/catalog/{bundled,optional}/<category>/<skill>/SKILL.md; packages/skills-catalog/generated/catalog.json is the generated manifest of catalog membership and metadata. A new SKILL.md under catalog/ = candidate new catalog skill — consult scripts/sync/detect-renames.mjs before treating a moved bundle as brand-new. Document new or changed catalog skills in the Skills reference (app-shipped catalog section) and the org Skills guide. catalog.json churn alone (reorder/regen) without a SKILL.md change is usually context-only.

watchers.name: schemas
watchers.detect: Zod / drizzle schema field additions, removals, or type changes on entities surfaced in docs (companies, agents, issues, routines, approvals, secrets).

watchers.name: web-ui
watchers.detect: UI component changes that may invalidate screenshots or end-user-facing guide flows. Cross-reference with screenshot registry depends_on entries before writing doc edits.

watchers.name: server-services
watchers.detect: Business logic changes that surface behavioural shifts users will notice (e.g. how agents interact, how approvals flow). Only produce doc edits when the change has user-visible effects, not pure refactors.

watchers.name: server-adapters
watchers.detect: Server-side adapter integrations (distinct from packages/adapters/*, which are the standalone adapter packages). Often relates to how the server hosts/proxies adapter capabilities. New top-level <name> dir under server/src/adapters/ = candidate new integration — consult scripts/sync/detect-renames.mjs before creating a new doc page.

watchers.name: db-migrations
watchers.detect: Migrations themselves rarely need user-facing docs, but a sudden burst of migrations often correlates with a schema change watched elsewhere. Use this watcher's hits as context only — never produce edits directly. Deliberately NOT promoted above context-only: most migrations are columns, indexes, and renames that need no prose, and promoting this would put all of them in front of a human for triage. The gap that would justify revisiting is a migration changing user-visible behaviour WITHOUT touching a packages/**/schema/*.ts file the `schemas` watcher already catches — a data backfill that changes a default, a retention window, or a constraint that starts rejecting input that used to be accepted.

watchers.name: release-channels
watchers.detect: The release-channel model (canary → nightly → beta → stable), its npm dist-tags and Docker image tags, and the `paperclipai channels` command. `doc/CHANNELS.md` is the authoritative parent guide; `channels.ts` holds the RELEASE_CHANNELS descriptors and the version→channel regexes. Changes here (a new lane, a dist-tag rename, the `:latest`-tracks-stable semantics) must flow into the channels sections of update-paperclip.md and the CLI installation page. Note: channels.ts is also matched by the cli-commands watcher — dedupe by surface, don't emit twice.
watchers.channel_context: Docs ship on the STABLE lane only. Do not describe beta/nightly/canary versions as the release; they are npm/Docker artifacts with no git tag. See maintenance/release-channels-plan.md.

watchers.name: release-notes
watchers.detect: Fetched via `gh release view <tag>` to give other watchers framing/intent. Never produces edits directly — release notes are reference data, not source.

adapter_doc_sources.$comment: Maps a doc basename (docs/reference/adapters/<name>.md) to the source paths the verifier should search. Use when the doc name does not match the adapter package directory under packages/adapters/. Without an entry here, verify-edit.mjs finds no sources and reports every adapter-config-field on the page as unverified — a silent false negative that fires on every run, not a one-off.

auto_merge_safety.$comment: forbid_kinds blocks auto-merge for destructive changes regardless of size. A 1-line rename is still a breaking change and demands human review. max_lines_changed=50 accommodates real-world env-vars batch additions (e.g. a new feature shipping with 10–20 related env vars and their inline comments in .env.example).

$notes.no_skip_patterns: We deliberately do NOT filter commits by message regex (e.g. ^revert, ^[codex]). The diff window is cumulative (last_release_tag → HEAD) so reverts are already net-zero in the manifest. Filtering by message would HIDE the undo signal — if we processed an original commit and then skipped its revert, docs would stay wrong forever. The proper filter is surface impact via watcher path globs.
$notes.quarantine_still_needed: Quarantine handles the race where a feature lands but its revert hasn't yet. Without it, we'd churn doc edits that get undone the next day.
